written: 2026-10-10, before the first run of any comparison below

inputs.space: scene-linear Rec.709 primaries, D65 white (the engine's working space)

cube.axis_rule: 0, then 2^(-10 + 17*(i-1)/31) for i = 1..32, rounded to float32

grey_ramp.rule: R = G = B = 2^(-12 + 20*k/255) for k = 0..255, rounded to float32

saturation_ramps.rule: for hue h in R, Y, G, C, B, M (unit RGB with components 0 or 1), level L in {0.18, 1, 8}, t = k/32 for k = 0..32: each component is float32(L) * ((1 - t) + t*h_c), one float32 multiply

inputs.generator: raw_native_cli colour grid OUT; the comparison tools and the GPU test read that file, so every implementation sees the same float32 inputs. Its SHA-256 is recorded with each result.

pipelines.clip/display-p3: Rec.709 to P3-D65 matrix, clamp, sRGB piecewise encoding
pipelines.clip/rec2020: Rec.709 to Rec.2020 matrix, clamp, BT.1886 inverse EOTF (pure 2.4)
pipelines.pbr-neutral/srgb: Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapper, then clip/srgb
pipelines.agx/srgb: AgX in the Filament and three.js form (inset matrix, log2 range -12.47393 to 4.026069 EV, 6th-order sigmoid polynomial, outset matrix), then clip/srgb
pipelines.aces2-sdr/srgb: Rec.709 to AP0 (Bradford), ACES 2.0 output transform at 100 nits with Rec.709 limiting primaries, clamp, sRGB piecewise encoding
pipelines.aces2-sdr/display-p3: as above with P3-D65 limiting primaries and P3-D65 encoding primaries
pipelines.aces2-hdr1000/rec2100-pq: ACES 2.0 at 1,000 nits with P3-D65 limiting primaries, clamp to peak, P3-D65 to Rec.2020 matrix, SMPTE ST 2084 encoding (1.0 = 100 nits)

ocio.version: OpenColorIO 2.6.0 (PyPI wheel opencolorio==2.6.0), run offline; never a build dependency

mapping.clip/srgb: ColorSpaceTransform 'Linear Rec.709 (sRGB)' to 'sRGB Encoded Rec.709 (sRGB)' in the built-in studio-config-latest, then clamp to [0,1]
mapping.clip/display-p3: 'Linear Rec.709 (sRGB)' to 'sRGB Encoded P3-D65', then clamp
mapping.clip/rec2020: 'Linear Rec.709 (sRGB)' to CIE XYZ D65, then built-in 'DISPLAY - CIE-XYZ-D65_to_REC.1886-REC.2020', then clamp
mapping.aces2-sdr/srgb: 'Linear Rec.709 (sRGB)' to 'ACES2065-1', built-in 'ACES-OUTPUT - ACES2065-1_to_CIE-XYZ-D65 - SDR-100nit-REC709_2.0', built-in 'DISPLAY - CIE-XYZ-D65_to_sRGB'

not_covered.pbr-neutral/srgb: OCIO 2.6.0 has no built-in PBR Neutral; checked against the Khronos specification's formula only
not_covered.agx/srgb: OCIO 2.6.0 has no built-in AgX; this is the Filament and three.js approximation, checked against its published constants only

bounds.gpu_vs_cpp: every channel of every input: |GPU 8-bit code - C++ 8-bit code| <= 1, after rounding each encoded value in [0,1] to round(255*v)

cpp_vs_ocio_sdr.metric: CIEDE2000 between the two encoded outputs, each decoded to display-linear light, converted to XYZ (D65) and CIELAB with the display white as reference white

cpp_vs_ocio_hdr.metric: Delta E ITP (ITU-R BT.2124) between the two PQ outputs decoded to absolute luminance

bounds.why: A CIEDE2000 of 1 is about one just-noticeable difference. The C++ ACES 2.0 is a float32 port of OCIO's own implementation, so differences should come only from matrix rounding and OCIO's fast-pow paths; 0.5 at worst leaves room for those and fails a real porting error. Clip pipelines are matrices and curves and should agree to rounding.

does_not_prove: Agreement with OCIO on these inputs, in these pipelines. Not agreement on negative or non-finite input, not the visual quality of any tone mapper, and not that a display shows these values.
